SMTO-TSK-0031 — This needs an earlier Agent task, and none was found

GUID: 3579a749-caf7-4b54-a81c-ed9e3ab3a5aa
Slug: task-request-id-required
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find an Agent task behind the message or conversation you picked. Older messages, or ones that never ran as an Agent task, can't be used for this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, choose Save to workflow beside a message that ran as an Agent task and shows its results. Only messages with a saved Agent task behind them can be copied into a workflow.
  2. If there is no such message, open Workflows, select New workflow, and type the prompt yourself. A new workflow doesn't need an earlier task to copy from.
  3. If you saw this while opening a conversation, check that you opened the right one. SMTO looked for the latest Agent task in that conversation and found none.

What success looks like

  • The workflow editor opens with your prompt filled in, or the conversation shows its latest task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't pick an unrelated message just to get past this; the workflow would then repeat that other message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The action needs a saved request ID linked to a native Agent run (capturing a request as a workflow, or reading a conversation's latest run), but the request ID is missing or no Agent run exists for that request or conversation.

What this means

  • A capture/control request has no saved request identifier or no retained native Agent run linked to the selected request/conversation. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A capture/control request has no saved request identifier or no retained native Agent run linked to the selected request/conversation.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the request-to-run link and supported history type; a trace alone may not contain a native run.

How to fix it

  • Supply a request_id whose trace links to a native Agent run in the selected conversation (check the conversation's native-conversations latest endpoint and the request's run link). Historical traces without a native run cannot be captured; create the workflow from a draft instead, or select a request that ran in Agent mode.
  • Open the owning saved request and select its retained Agent run. Historical records without a run cannot be used for this action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The action selects an owned saved request with the required retained Agent state.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
